findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() can now return null, contradicting the GroupModel contract
findings.description: The new body `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();` returns null when the backing group has vanished. The default method in server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/GroupModel.java:293-300 is documented "Never returns {@code null}." The JPA implementation (model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/GroupAdapter.java:190) always returns a count query result. The only caller, `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:89-92), passes the value straight into `setSubGroupCount`, so the null is silently serialized instead of surfacing as an error. Returning `0L` would keep the documented contract. If null is really intended, the GroupModel Javadoc must change to say so.

findings.title: Null handling for a vanished group is inconsistent across the same class
findings.description: The same race this change fixes still throws NPE in the three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268, which call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. The class already handles the same condition three different ways: `getDelegateForUpdate()` (line 60-61) throws `IllegalStateException`, `isUpdated()` (lines 73-74) throws `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")`, and the new `getSubGroupsCount` returns null. The fix covers only the count path that the new test exercises. Pick one policy and apply it to every `modelSupplier.get()` dereference in the class, or document why only the count path can race.

findings.title: Reader thread leaks and busy-loops forever if the deletion loop throws
findings.description: `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 is not in a `finally`. The reader thread (lines 139-149) is non-daemon and loops `while (!deletedAll.get())` with no pause. If any `remove()` at lines 152-154 throws, the flag is never set and the thread keeps issuing `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` for the rest of the JVM's life. Each read triggers a count query per top-level group through `populateSubGroupCount`. Each failure is appended to a `CopyOnWriteArrayList`, which copies the whole array on every add. Also, the `fail(...)` at line 131 skips deletion of groups already created, which leaves them in the managed realm. Wrap the deletion in try/finally that sets the flag and joins the thread, and make the thread a daemon.

findings.title: Assertion can run before the reader finishes, so late failures are missed
findings.description: The test asserts `caughtExceptions` at line 157 without joining the reader thread. A read in flight when the flag flips can add its exception after the assertion has already passed, so the test can report success despite a failed read. Nothing also guarantees the reader completed a single successful read, so the assertion can pass vacuously. Join the thread before asserting, and assert a successful-read counter is greater than zero. The final state of the realm is also never checked after deletion.

findings.title: The regression test depends on a timing race and does not deterministically cover the null branch
findings.description: The null path in `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount` is reached only when a group is removed between listing and counting. The test relies on that interleaving across 100 deletions, so it may pass against the pre-fix code on many runs. A stress test is reasonable for this scenario, but a unit-level test that gives the adapter a delegate lookup returning null would exercise the branch every time. I did not run the test, so I cannot say how often it reproduces.

findings.title: Test name, typo and whitespace drift
findings.description: `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` does not say what is asserted (no errors while listing during concurrent deletes). Neighboring tests such as `getGroupsWithBriefAndFullRepresentation` (line 853) name the behavior. The variable `groupUuuids` has a triple-u typo, used at lines 121, 129 and 152. Line 117 is a whitespace-only line before `@Test`.

findings.title: CachedGroup `@Override` on getRealm() is valid
findings.description: Verified that `InRealm` declares `String getRealm();` (model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/entities/InRealm.java:8). The annotation compiles and makes the interface contract explicit. No behavior change.

findings.title: Removed GroupUtils helper was unused private code
findings.description: A repo-wide search found no remaining references to `groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement` in `GroupUtils`. The only other match is a separately declared private method with a different signature in server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/ModelToRepresentation.java:209. Every remaining import in `GroupUtils` is still used.
